stem: A client feels inadequate about poor performance in one area of life and responds by devoting substantial effort to achieving success in a different area. Which defense mechanism does this best illustrate?
rationale: StatPearls defines compensation as focusing on achievement in one area of life to distract attention from inadequacy or fear of inadequacy in another area. The scenario directly matches this higher-level defense mechanism.
educational_objective: Recognize compensation as achievement in one domain used to offset perceived inadequacy in another.
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; article last updated May 22, 2023; accessed 2026-08-17
source_claim_supported: Defines compensation and provides an analogous example of shifting effort toward achievement in another area after perceived inadequacy.
correction_summary: Retained the compensation construct but shortened the stem and replaced cue-heavy distractors with other genuine defense mechanisms.
audit_findings: A uniquely matches the described achievement-offset pattern. B attributes one's traits to others; C reverts to earlier functioning; D redirects emotion to another target.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 / PDF p.14
